claims.statement: Child teams inherit their parent's access permissions. This is an inheritance dependency, not proof of actual team nesting, a complete effective-permission calculation, parent membership inheritance, or an authorization grant; the linked nested-team guide remains separate review work.

For a person who belonged to the organization within the preceding three months, the procedure presents restoration of privileges versus a fresh start. FPT/GHEC use invitation-and-reinstatement or invitation-and-fresh-start actions; the other branch uses addition-and-reinstatement or addition-and-fresh-start. The three-month condition is not indefinite retention or automatic restoration, and no acceptance or restored privilege was verified.

A user license is selected only when the organization belongs to an enterprise account with multiple licenses. This condition is not proof of license availability, a paid purchase, assigned entitlement, billing acceptance, or upstream distribution rights; no license was selected.

If the invitee has never belonged to the organization or their privileges were cleared, the flow calls for choosing a role and permits optional team additions. FPT/GHEC send an invitation; the other branch adds a member. These actions are not interchangeable evidence of accepted membership, effective team permissions, or a granted role.

The organization role selector is presented when the invitee has never been a member or prior privileges were cleared. The fragment does not identify eligible roles, authorize selecting an owner role, establish reinstated access, or provide a completed assignment receipt.

The left-sidebar Codespaces entry is navigation only. It proves neither feature availability, payer selection, running workspace, resource allocation, cost approval, nor a deployed organization policy.
